words.meaning: to make an adjustment so strong that it creates the opposite problem
words.example: After one late release, the team overcorrected by adding so many reviews that every update stalled.

words.meaning: to remove or hide sensitive information before sharing a document
words.example: Please redact the customer account numbers before sending the report outside the company.

words.meaning: to show that an idea, result, or claim is no longer valid or reliable
words.example: The missing records could invalidate our conclusion about the sales trend.

words.meaning: to reduce costs or operations during a difficult period
words.example: The company chose to retrench in two markets while protecting its core product.

words.meaning: to use an initial success or advantage to gain something greater
words.example: She parlayed a successful pilot project into a leadership role on the national rollout.

phrases.meaning: to apply strong pressure on someone to act or agree
phrases.example: The landlord put the screws to the contractor after the repairs fell weeks behind.

phrases.meaning: to have no idea who someone is
phrases.example: I don't know him from Adam, so I'm not comfortable giving him access to the office.

phrases.meaning: to remain deeply annoying or hard to accept
phrases.example: The way they took credit for her work really stuck in her craw.

phrases.term: six of one, half dozen of the other
phrases.meaning: used when two choices are effectively equal
phrases.example: We can drive downtown or take the train; with traffic today, it's six of one, half dozen of the other.

phrases.meaning: a warning not to be clever, evasive, or disrespectful
phrases.example: Don't get cute with me—just tell me why the invoice was never submitted.
